mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) at or below 0.25% compresses discount rates for equity valuation, generating positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days due to reduced cost of capital for corporate earnings.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 50% of instances when FEDFUNDS ≤ 0.25% over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5.0% signals robust labor market conditions that increase consumer spending and corporate profit margins, driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 40% of instances when UNRATE < 5.0% over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous growth in housing starts (HOUST) > 1% and retail sales (RSAFS) > 0.5% in the prior month indicates accelerating consumer demand, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 30% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS exceed thresholds over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in FEDFUNDS below 0.25% for 3+ months signals monetary easing, reducing risk-free rates and boosting equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in > 50% of instances during FEDFUNDS decline ≥ 0.25% over 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: Positive quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1) above 0.5% q/q indicates expanding economic activity, leading to rising corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day returns are negative in > 60% of instances when GDPC1 growth ≥ 0.5% q/q over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A drop in industrial production (INDPRO) below 105.0 signals weakening manufacturing activity, reducing corporate output and profit expectations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are positive in > 55% of instances when INDPRO < 105.0 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent payroll growth (PAYEMS) > 0.5% and unemployment decline (UNRATE) > 0.2% in the prior month indicate labor market strength, increasing consumer spending and positive S&P 500 returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day returns are negative in > 35% of instances when both PAYEMS and UNRATE thresholds are met over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion (GDP growth > 2.0% and UNRATE < 5.0%), rising housing starts (HOUST) above 1% signals sustained consumer demand, generating positive S&P 500 returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day returns are negative in > 45% of instances during late-cycle expansion when HOUST rises > 1% over any 2-year rolling window.
